meta.title: AeroTurbine | Clean air, powered by the exhaust (design demo)
meta.description: AeroTurbine is an off-grid exhaust interceptor concept. It makes its own power from exhaust and filters pollutants. Engineering design demo, not a finished product.

banner.text: Under development: this is a demo of the filter concept, not a finished or field-tested machine.

hero.title: AeroTurbine
hero.summary: Clean air, powered by the exhaust itself.
hero.badge: Stage: Engineering Design & Simulation Blueprint | Submitted to Harvard VISION 2026
hero.note: AeroTurbine is still being designed. This page shows a demo of the filter idea and an engineering blueprint. Every number here is a design target or a simulation value, not a measured result.
hero.target: Design target: up to 70% fewer pollutants and particulates.
hero.bgLabel: Decorative moving lines that suggest air flow

health.title: Why this matters locally
health.intro: Bad air makes people sick. It is a big problem in industrial areas.
health.globalLabel: Outdoor air pollution is linked to about this many early deaths every year worldwide:
health.placesText: Factories, traffic and diesel backup generators release these pollutants:
health.pollutants: PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO and VOCs
health.effectsTitle: What health studies link to PM2.5 and NO2
health.pmText: Each +10 µg/m³ is linked to about 10 to 20% higher heart disease and stroke deaths.
health.pmChart: Bar from 10% to 20% higher heart disease and stroke deaths
health.no2Text: Each +10 µg/m³ is linked to a relative risk of 1.09 for childhood asthma.
health.note: These are links found in health studies. They are not results from AeroTurbine.
health.failA1: They draw a lot of electricity.
health.failA2: Their sorbents stop working properly above 60 °C. Heat makes captured gas escape.
health.failB1: It makes its own power from the exhaust. Design target: up to 122.6 W.
health.failB2: Cooling fins bring the gas below 60 °C before it reaches the filter cartridge. This is the design intent.

blueprint.title: The 3-zone blueprint
blueprint.intro: Pick a zone to see what is inside. The arrow shows which way the gas flows.
blueprint.diagramLabel: Side-view diagram of the exhaust interceptor with three zones
steps: Hot exhaust enters. The spring-loaded bypass valve protects the engine.
The Venturi nozzle speeds the gas up. Two micro-turbines spin. The TEG collar adds power.
Additional catalytic stages clean NOx, CO and hydrocarbons (design concept).
Cooling fins bring the gas below 60 °C.
Layer 2, soda lime honeycomb, captures CO2 and SO2.
Layer 3, activated carbon, catches VOCs and other gas-phase toxins.
Cleaner gas leaves. Sensors compare the air before and after.

panel.label: Details
panel.ratioTitle: Cartridge: flow order and mass share
panel.ratioOrder: Gas flows through the layers in this order:
panel.ratioText: Mass ratio, soda lime : zeolite : carbon = 70:20:10
panel.catNote: Shown in the reference schematic only. No performance numbers are available.
panel.intent: Design intent: all layers fill up at about the same time, so there is one maintenance swap.

z1.title: Zone 1: Power harvesting
z1.plain: The exhaust spins small turbines and heats a collar. Both make electricity, so the device needs no power from the host engine.
components: Spring-loaded bypass valve. If backpressure rises above a safe limit (dP > dP_crit), it opens by itself so the host engine never stalls.
Venturi nozzle that speeds up the gas.
Thermoelectric generator (TEG) collar that uses the Seebeck effect.
z1.statsNote: All power values are design targets, not measured results. The total is meant to power the electronics with no host power.

z2.title: Zone 2: Cooling and filtration
z2.plain: Fins cool the gas first. Then it passes through a swappable cartridge with three layers.
components: External aluminum cooling fins cool the gas below 60 °C by natural convection.
Swappable 3-layer cartridge in an aluminum capsule.
Thermally insulated black rubber handle for tool-free swapping.

layers.name: Soda lime honeycomb
layers.role: CO2 reaction: Ca(OH)2 + CO2 → CaCO3 + H2O. Also scrubs SO2.

z2.statsNote: The 70% figure is a design target. A model also estimates 15 to 22% fewer asthma-related emergency room visits in nearby communities. That is a modeled estimate, not a measured result.

z3.title: Zone 3: Smart ECU
z3.plain: A small computer and battery sit on a cool outer wall. Sensors before and after the filter let it work out how well the filter is doing.
components: Upstream and downstream sensor sets (BME680 + Bosch BMV080 particulate sensor) to calculate filter efficiency in real time.
Isolated on a cool external wall.
z3.statsNote: Real-time efficiency is a design feature. It has not been field-tested.

valve.name: Spring-loaded bypass valve
valve.desc: Opens by itself if backpressure gets too high, so the host engine never stalls.

venturi.name: Venturi nozzle
venturi.desc: Narrows the pipe to speed up the gas so it can spin the turbines.

turbines.name: Two micro-turbines
turbines.desc: Spin one after the other in the fast gas. Design target: up to 50.6 W.

scr.name: Passive SCR catalyst
scr.desc: Reduces NOx with ammonia: NOx + NH3 → N2 + H2O. Design concept, no numbers yet.

urea.name: Solid-urea micro-dosing channel
urea.desc: Feeds a tiny amount of ammonia source to the SCR stage. Design concept.

ptpd.name: Pt/Pd oxidation catalyst
ptpd.desc: Turns CO and hydrocarbons into CO2 and water: CO + O2 → CO2 and HC + O2 → CO2 + H2O. Design concept.

fins.name: Cooling fins
fins.desc: Aluminum fins cool the gas below 60 °C by natural convection.

lime.name: Lime honeycomb cartridge
lime.desc: Soda lime layer. Captures CO2 and scrubs SO2. It is 70% of the cartridge mass.

carbon.name: Activated carbon cartridge
carbon.desc: Pleated carbon layer. Catches VOCs and gas-phase toxins. It is 10% of the cartridge mass.

ecu.name: ECU and battery
ecu.desc: ESP-32 controller and LiFePO4 battery, isolated on a cool outer wall.

sim.title: Live parameter simulator
sim.intro: Move the sliders and watch what changes. The formulas are simple and shown below.
sim.label: Theoretical simulation values from design targets, not measured data.
sim.days: Days since the last cartridge swap
sim.barLabel: Stacked bar of turbine and TEG power. The mark shows the 122.6 W maximum.
sim.swapDays: About {d} days of use left at these settings.
sim.swapNoUse: No use at these settings, so the cartridge is not wearing out.
sim.swapHot: Gas is above 60 °C at the cartridge. The sorbent works worse and may let gas escape. This is why cooling matters.
sim.swapCool: Gas is below 60 °C at the cartridge. Good.
formulaList: Turbine power = 50.6 W × flow^1.5, where flow is 0 to 1.
TEG power = 72.0 W × tempFactor × flow. tempFactor = (exhaust temperature − 100) ÷ 300, kept between 0 and 1.
Total power = turbine + TEG. The most it can reach is 50.6 + 72.0 = 122.6 W.
Daily energy (Wh) = total power (W) × operating hours.
filterHealth = (1 − 0.6 × load²) × heatFactor. Load is operating hours since the swap divided by 600 h, kept between 0 and 1. So without heat, health falls from 1 to 0.4 at saturation.
heatFactor = 1 when the cartridge gas is 60 °C or less. Above that it drops by 0.6 for every 40 °C, to a minimum of 0.4.
sim.assumptions: Demo assumptions, not design facts: the 100 to 400 °C hot-side range, the 600 h cartridge life and the heat penalty. They only make the demo move. Replace them with measured values once the prototype is tested.

economy.title: Frugal engineering and a circular loop
economy.intro: The goal is a low-cost unit that communities can afford and keep running.
economy.costNote: Costs are estimates and targets, not quotes.
economy.loopLabel: Circular loop diagram. Four steps repeat in a cycle.
loopSteps: Communities swap cartridges through a subscription.
Spent cartridges go to municipal recycling centers.
By-products (industrial gypsum, CaSO4) are sold to cement and wallboard makers.
The revenue helps buy fresh sorbent for new cartridges.
